payload.body: The maximum flow derivative (MFD) is a voice-quality parameter quantifying the peak rate of change of glottal flow within a glottal cycle, reported per cycle and aggregated over voiced frames. Given the glottal flow waveform g(n) and the fundamental period T0 from pitch tracking, MFD is computed as the maximum magnitude of the first derivative (or first difference) of g within each pitch-synchronous cycle, max |g(n+1) - g(n)|, then aggregated across cycles by the median or mean over the analyzed frames. Its parameters are: (1) the glottal flow waveform g(n) — the inverse-filtering estimate of the glottal source, (2) the fundamental period T0 from pitch tracking, which frames the per-cycle window, (3) the derivative operator — first difference or finite difference over the sampled flow, (4) the normalization choice — absolute units (volume per sample interval) or relative to the cycle's maximum flow, and (5) the cross-cycle aggregation (median or mean). A high MFD marks a sharp glottal closure (pressed, spiky phonation) and a low MFD marks a gradual closure (breathy phonation), with maintained reference ranges separating typical from disordered phonation. It is reported in standardized units and persists as a member of the voice-quality measurement map: implemented in voice-analysis toolkits (Praat, laryngology suites), documented in laryngology and speech-language pathology, and maintained alongside jitter, shimmer, and the phase quotients.
